scope: Research-grade written selections for the /verified/ desk. Prices are the desk's own originated fair prices (no bookmaker odds were read); every selection sits inside the -250…+10000 American band. Each write-up is hand-written (no template), names the selection explicitly, and every factual claim is tied to the official governing-body URL and the UTC time it was fetched. Nothing is inferred: if a fact was not returned by an official endpoint this session it is not used.

confidence_rule.high: originated probability >= 0.66, fair price inside the band, and every official indicator captured this session (record, home/away split, last-10 or form string, scoring/goaltending leader, ranking) points the same way; at least three independent official facts.
confidence_rule.medium: originated probability >= 0.58 inside the band, or a high-grade pick with one official indicator pointing the other way (noted as a caveat).
confidence_rule.low: everything else; low-grade selections are not given a write-up.

note_on_times: All start times are UTC as stored on the desk. Where the desk's stored time is itself an irregularity (PDC per-match times, URC 'Local' label, WST render) the official session time is given in the text instead.

picks.headline: Kaprizov's eleven goals and a 1-3-0 Saddledome record point one way
picks.text: Minnesota Wild to win in Calgary. Kirill Kaprizov already has eleven goals, more than any player on either roster, and Jesper Wallstedt owns six of the Wild's wins, so Minnesota (6-2-2, 31 scored, 25 conceded) arrive covered at both ends. Calgary are 2-6-0 with the joint-fewest goals in the league (17, level with Los Angeles) and 37 against, and the Saddledome has been no refuge: 1-3-0 at home, outscored 19-9. The Flames did stop the rot last time out, so this is a price rather than a certainty, but the straight moneyline at -243 is the play.

picks.headline: Three straight wins, three shutouts and a 90.6% penalty kill back Dallas
picks.text: Dallas Stars to beat Winnipeg. Dallas have won three in a row and are the hardest team in the league to score on: fourteen goals against in nine games on the official team summary, three shutouts, and a 90.6% penalty kill. Mikko Rantanen leads them with five goals and Jake Oettinger has four of the wins. Winnipeg arrive on a two-game losing run at 4-3-2 with more goals conceded (26) than scored (24), Kyle Connor's eight goals doing most of the work. Dallas have been better on the road (3-1-1) than at home (2-2-0), which keeps this at medium, but the moneyline at -163 is the side.

picks.text: Carolina Hurricanes to win in Edmonton at plus money.
